summary: Aermotor LS-40 60-foot tower dated circa 1952-53 in Hampshire County, WV; disposed of by the state by 2017, now on private land, visits by landowner permission.

facts.design: Aermotor LS-40 7x7 all-steel cab on a 60-foot tower

access.note: Access by permission of the landowner, per the NHLR page.

facts.agency: Private landowner (disposed of by the WV Division of Forestry by 2017)

events.note: Visitor comment says the site has been used for fire observation since 1916
Register gives circa 1952-53; a visitor comment says the current tower was built in 1952
Disposed of from the WV Division of Forestry inventory by 2017; now on private land

evidence.supports: Visitor comment: fire observation since 1916; current tower and ground cabin built 1952
evidence.quote: The site at Ben's Knob has been used for fire observation since 1916, but the current 60-foot Aermotor LS-40 and ground cabin were built in 1952.
Ben's Knob Fire Tower is an Aermotor LS-40 7x7 all steel cab and 60 foot tower constructed circa 1952-53.
Last staffing by the West Virginia Division of Forestry is unknown.

evidence.supports: Disposed of by 2017; now on private land
evidence.quote: By 2017, it had been disposed from the Division's inventory and is located on private land.

evidence.supports: A residence cabin may survive on the property
evidence.quote: A residence cabin may survive on the property as well.

evidence.supports: Boards intact and glass remains in the cab (visitor comment)
evidence.quote: as all the boards are still intact, and some glass still remains in the cab.

evidence.supports: Pine trees around the tower; views out on all four sides
evidence.quote: you can still see out all four sides of the tower, as the trees rise up around the corners.
Bens Knob Hampshire 39.25772 -78.52591 Tower Standing NHLR US 1696, WV 27

evidence.supports: Visitor comment: pine trees now surround the tower
evidence.quote: the tower is mostly overtaken by the pine trees surrounding it

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Register's Built field and description give 1952-53; a visitor comment says the current tower was built in 1952. The story reports both.

notes_for_editor: Only two sources, both lists or registers; no state disposal record was found. height_m is the 60-foot figure converted. The NHLR photo credit (Rocco Germani) has no stated license, so no photo was added. The visitor comment is an NHLR contributor's text, not an official record.
